newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Monday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. August personal income/consumption, September Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) and August new homes sales data.
Personal income for August is forecast to show an increase of 0.6 percent compared with a 0.1 percent gain reported in July.
August personal consumption is expected to rise 0.5 percent against July's 0.2 percent hike.
The Chicago PMI for September is expected to ease to 56.0 percent from 60.0 percent in August.
August new home sales for is expected to be around 744,000 versus July's 783,000 units.

"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments. The market is now waiting for possible direction from tonight's personal income/consumption, Chicago PMI and new home sales figures," a local dealer said.
"But the numbers have been built into the market and most people are waiting for Friday's employment report, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday rose 5/8 percentage point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent and Tuesday/Wednesday rose 1/8 point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from last Friday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.
Three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, but six-months eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
